clue.text: Noise abates — in spite of them?

definitions.text: Noise abates — in spite of them?

parts.note: a row is a loud din or racket
dies, as a sound that dies away, means fades or abates

explanation.surface: A quiet falls despite the presence of a troublesome gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue points at the troublemakers whose din one would expect to persist: the quiet comes in spite of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy troublemakers are the people whose racket would normally stop any quiet from settling.

clue.text: Welsh carrier gets unpleasant customer

parts.note: to welsh on a deal is to rat on it, going back on one's word
a carrier is a carrier bag

explanation.surface: A Welsh airline or haulier is landed with a difficult client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' looks like the nationality but is the verb welsh, to renege.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratbag is British slang for a nasty, troublesome person, a rotter.

clue.text: Women's laughter, grasping revolutionary maxim with late reference

indicators.note: grasping means the laughter holds the next element inside it

parts.note: each woman (W) gives her laugh (HO), so women's laughter is two of these together

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the maxim word is read backwards

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or maxim

explanation.surface: A group of women laughs at an inflammatory slogan with an old citation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the maxim round to sit inside the two laughs; the plural 'Women' supplies a W for each laugh. 'late' means dead, as in the late author.
explanation.definitionFit: This British reference book lists biographies of the dead, the people once in its sister volume.

clue.text: I've gone by old artistic method

parts.note: someone who has gone by might say 'I'm past'

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having passed an old-fashioned way of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've gone by' reads as I'M PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painter's technique of laying paint on thickly so brushstrokes stand out.

clue.text: Rogue has issue to do with weapon

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
of a gun means belonging to or concerning a firearm

explanation.surface: A villain's son is in trouble over a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: This old exclamation and nickname refers affectionately to a scamp or rascal.

clue.text: Material preventing ladders or rakes touching roof

indicators.note: touching means the first piece sits directly against the next one

parts.note: a rip is an old word for a dissolute man, a rake, so rakes are rips
the top of a building is its roof

explanation.surface: Fabric that stops tights laddering, or a stack of garden rakes leaning on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladders here are runs or tears in fabric, as in stockings; 'rakes' looks like garden tools but means dissolute men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripstop is a woven fabric reinforced so that small tears cannot spread across it.

clue.text: Defying odds, Mr Big yearly provides foreign cash

indicators.note: defying the odd letters means ignoring them, taking only the even ones

explanation.surface: Against all odds, a gangster's annual haul supplies overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of MR BIG YEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The riyal is the currency of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and other Gulf states.

clue.text: Hot pastry rings preserve temperature

indicators.note: rings means the pastry word encircles the following pieces

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish
to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: Pastry rings help keep a hot dish warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like a noun but is the verb, to encircle.
explanation.definitionFit: Picante means spicy in Spanish, used of sauces with a peppery, fiery flavour.

clue.text: Rate obtained by worker maybe filling in cipher

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker covering for someone
a cipher is a zero, written as a nought

explanation.surface: A pay rate secured by a worker who fills in code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cipher' suggests a code but here means nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or pace at which something happens, especially music.

clue.text: Work sung with lisp, making you cross

indicators.note: work as a verb means to knead or shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone singing with a lisp is exasperating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges SUNG and LISP together; 'cross' is not angry but the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol for addition is shaped like an upright cross.

clue.text: Cheap and tinny, without copy for one

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the new letters take the place of the named one in the word tinny

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
W/O is the standard shorthand for without
to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: Something is dismissed as cheap, flimsy and tinny, lacking even a copy to compare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' asks for WOAPE (WO plus APE) to replace the I in TINNY, giving T + WOAPE + NNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available two for a penny is so plentiful as to be almost worthless, hence cheap.

clue.text: Essential to tour my constituency — backward part of UK

indicators.note: backward means the run of letters found is then read from right to left
the essential part of a phrase is its inner core, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A politician insists it is vital to visit every part of the constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential to' picks URMYC from inside 'tour my constituency'; 'backward' turns it round. CYMRU is the Welsh name for Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Welsh-language name for Wales, one of the four nations making up the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Confession of one slow to run up?

definitions.meaning: a dim-witted person admitting 'I am an idiot' would say, split up, that they are a donkey
to run up debts or a collection is to gather or pile them up

explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM ASS, the word is what a slow-witted person might confess: '(I) am (an) ass'.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or pile up a quantity is to run it up, as with a bill or a fortune.

clue.text: Foul: one is treated as a crime

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed and worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the word is

explanation.surface: A referee rules that a foul is to be prosecuted as a criminal offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges the letters of FOUL, ONE and IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious describes conduct of the nature of a felony, a serious offence under the law.

clue.text: Daydreaming in court and large meeting

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a gathering is a meeting of people

explanation.surface: Someone's mind wanders during a court hearing and a big assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes idle fantasising, likened to aimlessly collecting stray tufts of fleece from hedges.

clue.text: Extraordinarily, a horse is in a TT race on island

indicators.note: extraordinarily suggests something out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, called horse

explanation.surface: Remarkably, a horse is entered in the Isle of Man TT motorbike race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man, which makes 'island' look like part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The native Polynesian people of Tahiti form a distinct race or people of that island.

clue.text: Finery ordered by one direct

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, rearranged

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Fine clothes chosen by an individual who speaks plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges FINERY.
explanation.definitionFit: This slang term means aggressively forthright and confrontational, blunt and unsubtle.

clue.text: Shiny silver paper on the ground?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is rubbish such as paper dropped on the ground

explanation.surface: Silver wrapping paper glints on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering and sparkling, something that gleams brightly is shining.

clue.text: Plant produces substance that's sticky, and dry piece bird's eaten

parts.note: goo is any sticky, gloopy substance

indicators.note: the word dry has eaten the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a king is a chess piece
a hen is a bird; the 's here is 'has'

explanation.surface: A plant oozes a sticky substance, and a bird has eaten a dry morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'bird's eaten' as 'has eaten': the word dry swallows the chess piece and the bird. 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Good King Henry is a leafy perennial of the goosefoot family, once grown as a pot herb.

clue.text: Bruckner's Fifth, perfectly fine, covered in live music entertainment

indicators.note: the fifth points to the letter in fifth position of the composer's name
covered in means one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: are means live, exist, as in 'we are'
A-OK means perfectly all right

explanation.surface: A Bruckner symphony, flawlessly performed live, is great entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bruckner's Fifth' suggests a symphony but means the letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is entertainment in which amateurs sing along to recorded backing tracks.

clue.text: Prisoner upset with officer's initial refusal

indicators.note: upset means turned over; in a down clue the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
and means with, along with

indicators.note: initial points to the first letter of officer

explanation.surface: An inmate is distressed when an officer at first refuses him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CON into NOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase means 'it cannot be done', a flat refusal.

clue.text: Saving player's energy with a rest

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A player gets back their energy by resting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' is a keeper's saves, not conserving energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The goalkeeper is the team member whose job is to stop shots going in.

clue.text: "Engrave" spout holding carbon pipe up

parts.note: engrave in its rare literal sense means put in a grave, that is bury or inter

indicators.note: holding means the next element is held inside the spout word

parts.note: a jet is a spout of water or gas
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: An instruction to carve, a fountain spout with carbon deposits and a pipe that rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag 'Engrave' in its archaic sense of burying, not carving.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe up is to speak suddenly into a conversation, breaking in with a remark.

clue.text: Port and whisky in centre under barrel

indicators.note: under means in this down entry the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

indicators.note: in centre points to the middle letters of the word whisky

explanation.surface: Port and whisky sit in the middle of a cellar beneath a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' is not the wine but a harbour city, the capital of Tunisia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia, a harbour city on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Do well's Roman figures in steel, not stone

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in means the figures are placed inside what remains of the metal word
not means the stone abbreviation is dropped from the metal word

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Roman numerals cast in steel, not carved in stone, are a fine achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not stone' removes the weight abbreviation from the metal, leaving EEL for the numerals to go into. A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding or perform exceptionally well.

clue.text: Reactionary old police reading in PC perhaps something odd

indicators.note: reactionary hints at going backwards, so the old police force's letters are reversed

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001
I/O, input/output, covers a computer reading data in and writing it out

explanation.surface: Politically backward officers from the old force read out a quirky item in a constable's report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC perhaps' hints at a police constable but means a personal computer. The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a curious or unusual object prized as a novelty.

clue.text: Western companion as well to keep name quiet, ultimately

indicators.note: to keep means the outer word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: too means also or as well

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word quiet

explanation.surface: Someone also wants a name kept secret, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonto is the Lone Ranger's companion in the American Western stories.
explanation.definitionFit: In the classic American cowboy serial, this character rides beside the masked Lone Ranger.

clue.text: Bond: he reportedly rings to offer protection

parts.note: a chain is a bond or fetter

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it would be heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: he refers to a man, a male

explanation.surface: James Bond rings round to arrange some protection, or so the report goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007 but is a fetter. 'rings' is a noun: the linked metal rings of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: This armour is made of small interlocking metal rings that shielded medieval soldiers.

clue.text: Philosopher's career curtailed by cheat

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, losing the final letter

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong
a sell is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A thinker's professional life was cut short by a fraudster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun (a job) but is the verb, to rush. Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was the twentieth-century British logician and thinker who co-wrote Principia Mathematica.

clue.text: Well I never did meet son, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at an unlucky encounter with one's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges MEETSON.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation, popular as a British catchphrase, expresses astonishment just as that phrase does.
